title: 2nd Sitting of third session of 2025
summary: The sitting opened at 09:01 with 30 members counted present. Written replies from the Health and Home ministers on the state-run optical shop at IGMH, the national drug policy and the drug agency's acting CEO were tabled, and an urgent motion by the South Galolhu member on police use of a long-range acoustic device at the 3 October protest was not allowed onto the floor (12 for, 40 against). Members then debated a bill to amend the Land Transport Act (tougher fines, unlicensed driving, vehicle owners' liability, emergency vehicles), with several MDP and PNC members also trading blame over the 3 October protest. After a break, debate on the government's Re-employment Bill continued and a resolution on the Auditor General's Fenaka Corporation special audit was introduced; both carry on into part 2. This part continues the debate on a resolution before the Majlis. The member for North Galolhu speaks in support and argues that corruption, including in public-sector hiring, political spending and overseas medical costs, should be stopped. The member for Gan raises a point of order saying corruption is not a matter for this debate, and the chair asks the first member to continue. With many members still wanting to speak and several committees due to meet, the chair said the debate would be deferred, ended the day's agenda and set the next sitting for Tuesday 7 October 2025 at 9:00. The text layer is garbled in places, so some details and the exact resolution were not clear from this part.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Asked the Health Minister why the state opened an optical shop at IGMH, what it cost, and whether private optical businesses were studied first.
Asked the Home Minister when the national drug policy would be finished and why the National Drug Agency has an acting CEO.
Presented his Land Transport Act amendments: tougher penalties for unsafe driving, third-party insurance for injured people, and road space for emergency vehicles.
Supports the resolution in general and says corruption must be audited and stopped, including hiring of staff in state companies and government offices.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Tabled an urgent motion on police use of a long-range acoustic device against the 3 October protest, citing the lack of published rules for its use.
On the transport bill, said public order needs more than penalties, called for police rules on the device to be published, and urged release of those arrested.
In the Re-employment Bill debate, questioned the president's nomination of a judge to the Tax Appeal Tribunal, saying it affects public trust.

speakers.name: Dr. Ahmed Shamheed
positions: Supported the emergency-vehicle clause, citing a constituent whose life was saved because an emergency vehicle could be driven quickly.
Asked for more offences to be added, such as driving while impaired or using a phone, and for 'driving without a licence' to be clearly defined.
Questioned whether the fine range of MVR 10,000 to 50,000 is proportionate and whether the police device suits crowded roads.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: On the transport bill, said the state has no plan for traffic, questioned a Transport Ministry's role, criticised vehicle registration costs and defended the right to protest.
On the Re-employment Bill, backed the idea but cautioned against politically motivated hiring and double pay for pension recipients re-employed by government.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Criticised police closing roads during the 3 October protest and said roads belong to all users, including taxis and public transport.
Backed the aim of the amendments but raised parking near mosques, new foreign drivers' licences and the release of arrested MDP members.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Supported most amendments and the fine range for unlicensed driving, but opposed holding an owner's licence for 3 to 6 months when someone else drives their vehicle.

speakers.name: Hussain Hameed
positions: Praised police conduct on 3 October and backed the amendments.
Proposed that a new vehicle be registered in Male' only if another is disposed of, and that vehicle speed be capped at 30 km/h.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported the bill overall but said enforcement and Male' road capacity decisions matter more than bigger fines.
Argued the government's added taxis and approach to registration fees worsen congestion.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Supported the bill, which he said followed serious accidents, and urged the committee to consult agencies and consider different fees or insurance rules for atolls versus Male'.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said riders use the wrong lane on new bridges, including in Addu City, contrary to the law, and asked committees to consult traffic police and transport officials.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Backed the bill, noting changes to fines and owner liability, and said MDP's opposition to a member's own amendment was surprising.
Said MPs should model respect for the law, referring to the 3 October protest.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Naseem
positions: Supported the bill but said road-safety awareness programmes must actually run for new penalties to improve safety.

speakers.name: Hassan Mufeed Abdul Gadir
positions: Backed the Re-employment Bill, saying it lets retirees who want to keep working serve the state and gives experienced people who left jobs a chance to return.

speakers.name: Mohamed Fazeel
positions: Raised a point of order that the previous speaker was not speaking about the bill under debate.

speakers.name: Yoosuf Nasheed
positions: Raised a point of order that the corruption remarks were not a matter of order, and that those who looted should be questioned.

decisions: Urgent motion on police use of a long-range acoustic device was not taken up for debate (12 for, 40 against).
Three proposed changes to the Rules of Procedure (items 6.1 to 6.3) were sent to the General Committee for study.
The bill to amend the Constitution had its first reading announced.
Initial debate on the Land Transport Act amendment bill was held; no decision recorded in this part.
Written ministerial replies on the IGMH optical shop, the national drug policy and the drug agency's acting CEO were tabled and published without amendment.
The chair deferred the debate on the resolution because many members still wished to speak and several committees were scheduled to meet.
The sitting was closed and the next sitting set for Tuesday 7 October 2025 at 9:00.
